First tagged release. Magpie finds every image, video and audio file a page
loads or references, groups them by similarity, and downloads them in bulk.

**Install:** download `magpie-0.2.0.zip` below, unzip it, then
`chrome://extensions` → **Developer mode** → **Load unpacked** → choose the
folder. Chrome 120+. It also loads in Arc, Dia, Brave and Edge, though none of
those has been launched against it.

Not on the Chrome Web Store yet.

## What it does

Four detection layers feed one per-tab index: a `webRequest` observer, a
MAIN-world interceptor that mines the JSON an app fetches, a DOM scanner
covering `srcset`, `picture`, lazy `data-*` attributes, CSS backgrounds,
inline `<svg>`, `<canvas>` and gallery links, and HAR import. Anything two
layers agree on is `confirmed` and sorts first.

The signature interaction is **similarity selection**: pick one image and
Magpie selects every other item on the page that belongs to the same set -
same DOM structure, same URL shape, same dimensions - and downloads them
together. Thumbnails are resolved to their full-size originals, each candidate
proved with a `HEAD` request before it is offered.

`explore` walks the app on its own: it scrolls each page so lazy loaders fire,
opens the tabs, accordions and menus that hide more media, and follows
same-origin links most-like-the-start-page first. It is bounded by
construction and deliberately careful about what it clicks.

HLS and DASH manifests are parsed in-process and turned into a `yt-dlp` or
`ffmpeg` command. **Magpie never circumvents DRM and contains no code path
that could.**

## Since the untagged 0.1.1

This release is mostly the result of reading the whole tree against what the
README claims. Almost every fault below was a gap between a claim and its
implementation, and each was reproduced before it was fixed.

**Safety, and the two hard boundaries**

- A third-party iframe could steer the crawl off the site: explore messages
  went to every frame, so an ad frame's links were same-origin *to the ad
  network* and the tab was navigated there.
- The DRM boundary held only for the spellings we happened to write. A
  namespace-prefixed `<cenc:ContentProtection>` was invisible, so a Widevine
  manifest parsed as clean; an `#EXT-X-KEY` with no `METHOD` cleared the flag;
  `KEYFORMAT` was matched only by UUID.
- A `<button form="pay">` sitting outside its form was neither "a submit
  button" nor "inside a form", so the explorer would press it.
- Percent-encoding walked through the destructive-address check.

**Media that was silently lost**

- The dedupe key merged different assets: `?id=1001` and `?id=2002` were one
  photo, and the second URL was discarded.
- `srcset` was split on `,` - which sits inside every Cloudinary transform and
  every `data:` URI - and the resulting fragment *replaced* the working URL.
  The same function let `2x` outrank `1600w`.
- Layer B went silent on a revisited single-page-app route.

**Things that did not work**

- The side panel never opened from a right-click: `sidePanel.open()` sat
  behind two storage round-trips, so it lost the user gesture every time.
- Pressing Stop froze the progress counter and then said nothing, and reported
  every cancelled download as a failure.
- A batch did not survive the service worker being terminated, which one large
  file is enough to cause.

**Also fixed:** a page could hang the panel with its title alone, a HAR with
one odd field lost every other entry, an oversized HAR body exhausted memory,
the panel scrolled itself back to the top four times a second, Enter on a tile
started a download, Cmd-A was hijacked, and a URL *fragment* was enough to
make any link a "stream" the drawer would fetch.

## Verified

161 unit tests, a service-worker smoke test and two end-to-end runs against a
real Chrome, green locally and on CI. This release also unpacks the published
zip and registers its worker from *that*, so a packaging mistake cannot reach
you.

Known and not done: no test drives the context menu, HAR import is tested only
against a synthetic archive, and no commercial DRM player has been visited.
The README lists these in full under "Not verified".
